title: Infrastructure OSINT: Reverse DNS (PTR), BGP Anycast Geolocation & RADB Route Registry (AS397273)
summary: Investigated network routing and edge infrastructure behind radblok.co.za following Udemy lecture 22. Performed reverse DNS resolution (PTR records under in-addr.arpa) discovering ip-216-24-57-1.ingress.render.com and AWS Route 53 zone authority. Audited ASN metadata via ipinfo.io revealing BGP Anycast deployment with San Francisco origin registration, and queried the Routing Assets Database (RADB) to map AS397273's announced prefixes (74.220.56.0/24 and 216.24.57.0/24) with RPKI validation status.

sections.h: Forward & Reverse DNS Resolution Mechanics (PTR & in-addr.arpa)

blocks.text: Transitioning from domain OSINT into network reconnaissance, probed `radblok.co.za` using forward and reverse DNS lookups:

blocks.label: kali (nslookup)
blocks.text:
┌──(general㉿lee)-[~]
└─$ nslookup radblok.co.za
Server:		192.168.0.1
Address:	192.168.0.1#53

Non-authoritative answer:
Name:	radblok.co.za
Address: 216.24.57.1

┌──(general㉿lee)-[~]
└─$ nslookup 216.24.57.1
1.57.24.216.in-addr.arpa	name = ip-216-24-57-1.ingress.render.com.

Authoritative answers can be found from:
57.24.216.in-addr.arpa	nameserver = ns-1359.awsdns-41.org.
57.24.216.in-addr.arpa	nameserver = ns-1789.awsdns-31.co.uk.
57.24.216.in-addr.arpa	nameserver = ns-323.awsdns-40.com.
57.24.216.in-addr.arpa	nameserver = ns-662.awsdns-18.net.

Notice the DNS mechanics: In IPv4, reverse lookups query the special `.in-addr.arpa` tree with octets reversed (`1.57.24.216`). The PTR record immediately unmasks the underlying PaaS ingress host (`ingress.render.com`) and reveals that Render's reverse zone is delegated to Amazon Route 53 nameservers (`awsdns`).
Queried IP intelligence for `216.24.57.1` to evaluate ASN registration and geographical presence:

head: Attribute
Value
Technical & Reconnaissance Meaning
rows: Autonomous System Number (ASN) assigned to Render Services Inc. Provides the key identifier for BGP routing table mapping.
**BGP Anycast Routing**. Explains why geolocation indicates San Francisco, CA while physical latency is ~3ms in South Africa: multiple global edge locations announce this identical IP.
Confirms this node acts as a shared multi-tenant ingress load balancer for Render custom domains.

sections.h: Routing Assets Database (RADB) & BGP Prefix Mapping

blocks.text: Queried the Internet Routing Registry (IRR) via RADB (`whois.radb.net`) to enumerate all IP prefixes originated by AS397273:

blocks.label: kali (radb query)
blocks.text:
┌──(general㉿lee)-[~]
└─$ whois -h whois.radb.net -- '-i origin AS397273'
route:          74.220.56.0/24
origin:         AS397273
descr:          Proxy add for Render to re-advertise upstream
mnt-by:         MAINT-AS14380
changed:        brad@opusinteractive.com 20260406
source:         RADB
rpki-ov-state:  not_found

route:          216.24.57.0/24
origin:         AS397273
descr:          655 5th St #19, San Francisco CA 94107
mnt-by:         MNT-RS-1125
source:         ARIN
rpki-ov-state:  valid

route:          216.24.57.0/24
descr:          RPKI ROA for 216.24.57.0/24 / AS397273
max-length:     24
origin:         AS397273
source:         RPKI

1. **Prefix Discovery**: Render announces two primary /24 CIDR blocks: `74.220.56.0/24` (upstream transit via Opus Interactive) and `216.24.57.0/24` (direct ARIN assignment).
2. **RPKI Validation (`valid`)**: `216.24.57.0/24` has a cryptographically signed Route Origin Authorization (ROA), protecting against BGP prefix hijacking attacks.
